segment: NSW residential sales agencies (principals, sales agents, project marketers) and home builders (volume, custom, off-the-plan) who would pay SHOWHAUS monthly; plus 3 outside-segment payers
grounding: Australian listing marketing is mostly vendor-paid (VPA): agents pass per-listing costs to the vendor, so a monthly agency fee competes with the agency's own margin, not the vendor's budget.

Competitor offer wording (littlehinges.com.au sales agents page, read 2026-11-27): '3D Virtual Tour + Videos + Photography + Floorplan', 'Enable sight unseen buyers to inspect anytime', claims of '300%' engagement and '95%' more likely to call quoted from Matterport / realestate.com.au.
Domain x Matterport partnership (agent.domain.com.au) means many Sydney agents already know camera-scanned 3D tours and their per-listing price.
Reddit r/realtors could not be read directly from this session (HTTP 403 through the proxy); quotes below come from vendor pages and earlier SHOWHAUS panels, so this panel is weaker on real voices.

personas.text: Karen, 52, principal of a 6-agent independent agency in Randwick. Lists about 9 homes a month, median $2.4M. Pays a photographer + floorplan $650 per listing, billed to the vendor. Last time a proptech rep pitched her (a virtual staging app) she took a free trial, never logged in again, and cancelled after 2 months. Cares about winning listings at the appraisal, not about buyer tech.

Tony, 61, owns a LJ Hooker franchise in Penrith. 14 listings a month, mostly $700k–$1.1M houses. Deletes most software emails unread. Last year signed a 12-month CRM add-on he regrets. Thinks 'buyers come to the open home anyway, 3D is for the out-of-towners'. Wants every cost passed to the vendor.

Priya, 34, top sales agent at a Ray White office in Parramatta, runs her own Instagram, 4 listings a month. Pays for her own social ads. Last time she tried a 3D tour (Matterport via the photographer) she liked it but the vendor balked at the extra $300. Wants anything that helps her win the appraisal pitch against other agents.

Ben, 29, junior agent at a Belle Property office on the Lower North Shore, 2 listings a month. Has no budget authority; his principal approves all spend. Last time he forwarded a tool to his principal it was ignored. Sceptical of anything 'AI generated' because buyers complained about a virtually staged photo that misrepresented a room.

Mei, 41, director of a project-marketing agency selling off-the-plan apartments in Wolli Creek and Arncliffe for mid-size developers. Spends $40k+ per project on CGI renders and a display suite. Last project she commissioned a Unity walkthrough for $18k that took 10 weeks. Cares about buyers from overseas who can't visit.

Grant, 48, sales director for a developer's in-house team in Western Sydney (townhouses, 30-60 lots per stage). Uses the same render studio for every stage. Last time a startup offered a cheaper visualisation, the quality embarrassed him in front of the developer. Will not put anything 'not photoreal' in front of buyers.

Hannah, 38, marketing manager at a volume home builder with 40 house designs and 9 display homes across Sydney. Already has floor plans for every design. Spends on Facebook leads to display villages. Last time she bought a tool it was a $1,200/month interactive-floorplan subscription she cancelled because sales staff didn't use it.

Steve, 55, owns a custom/knock-down-rebuild builder in Sutherland Shire, 12 homes a year, gets work by referral. Draws plans with an outside drafter. Has never paid a monthly fee for marketing. Last time a client couldn't picture a plan he walked them through it with a pencil.

Daniel, 36, runs a design-and-build firm in the Hills District, 20 builds a year, active on Instagram with reels of finished homes. Pays $2k per project for 3D renders from a freelancer. Last client lost confidence mid-build because the kitchen looked bigger in the render.

Robyn, 58, principal of a 3-agent agency in Orange (Regional NSW). 5 listings a month, many buyers relocating from Sydney who drive 3.5 hours to inspect. Watches every dollar; marketing is vendor-paid. Last time she paid a monthly fee it was for a website she still pays for and rarely updates.

Marcus, 44, principal of a 15-agent boutique in the Eastern Suburbs (Bondi/Coogee apartments). Has a marketing coordinator. Pays for Pricefinder, realestate.com.au Premiere and a video team. Last time he adopted new tech (digital appraisal reports) it was because a competitor used it first.

Lisa, 46, agent at an independent agency in Campbelltown, 3 listings a month, happy with photos + floor plan + video. Thinks realestate.com.au is the only marketing that matters. Last time she tried a 'free first listing' offer the provider took 9 days and the listing was already under offer.

Aaron, 39, head of property management at a Sydney agency, 280 managed rentals, 25 re-leases a month. Lets the tenant-facing side run on templates. Last time he tried a virtual inspection tool tenants still asked for in-person viewings.

Sophie, 33, interior designer and stylist who stages homes for sale in the Inner West, 6 jobs a month for agents. Would love buyers to see her furniture layouts. Last time she used a room-planner app the scale was wrong and she lost a day.

Nathan, 42, buyers agent with interstate and overseas clients buying in Sydney; shortlists 20 homes a month for clients who can't inspect. Pays for CoreLogic and his own time. Last time a client bought sight unseen they were upset about aircraft noise nobody mentioned.

Joe, 63, small developer doing duplexes and terrace builds in Canterbury-Bankstown, 3 projects a year, sells off the plan through a local agent. Pays nothing he can avoid. Last time he paid for renders the agent never used them.
